stem:
Iodine monochloride, $\text{ICl}$, is a yellow-brown gas. It reacts with hydrogen gas under certain conditions as shown.

$$2\text{ICl(g)} + \text{H}_2\text{(g)} \rightarrow 2\text{HCl(g)} + \text{I}_2\text{(g)}$$

Experiments are performed using different starting concentrations of $\text{ICl}$ and $\text{H}_2$. The initial rate of each reaction is measured. The following results are obtained.

| experiment | $[\text{ICl}]/\text{mol dm}^{-3}$ | $[\text{H}_2]/\text{mol dm}^{-3}$ | relative rate of reaction |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | $4.00 \times 10^{-3}$ | $4.00 \times 10^{-3}$ | 1.00 |
| 2 | $4.00 \times 10^{-3}$ | $7.00 \times 10^{-3}$ | 1.75 |
| 3 | $4.00 \times 10^{-3}$ | $1.00 \times 10^{-2}$ | 2.50 |
| 4 | $5.00 \times 10^{-3}$ | $8.00 \times 10^{-3}$ | 2.50 |
| 5 | $7.00 \times 10^{-3}$ | $8.00 \times 10^{-3}$ | 3.50 |

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Identify a change, taking place in the reaction mixture, that would enable measurements of the rate of this reaction to be made.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Use the data in the table to show that the reaction is first order with respect to $\text{H}_2\text{(g)}$.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Use the data in the table to show that the reaction is first order with respect to $\text{ICl(g)}$.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text: Complete the rate equation for the reaction between $\text{ICl(g)}$ and $\text{H}_2\text{(g)}$.

parts.label: (e)
parts.text: Use experiment 3 to calculate a numerical value for the rate constant, $k$.

parts.label: (f)
parts.text:
The reaction $2\text{ICl(g)} + \text{H}_2\text{(g)} \rightarrow 2\text{HCl(g)} + \text{I}_2\text{(g)}$ is first order with respect to $\text{ICl(g)}$ and first order with respect to $\text{H}_2\text{(g)}$.

Suggest a mechanism for this reaction. You should assume

- the mechanism has two steps,
- the first step is much slower than the second step.

$$\text{first step} \quad \ldots\ldots \rightarrow \ldots\ldots$$

$$\text{second step} \quad \ldots\ldots \rightarrow \ldots\ldots$$

parts.label: (g)(i)
parts.stem: An alternative method is used to show that the reaction is first order with respect to $\text{H}_2\text{(g)}$. This method uses a large excess of $\text{ICl(g)}$ and measures how the concentration of $\text{H}_2\text{(g)}$ varies with time.
parts.text: Describe two ways of using these results to show the reaction is first order with respect to $\text{H}_2\text{(g)}$ concentration.

parts.label: (g)(ii)
parts.text: Explain the reason for using a large excess of $\text{ICl(g)}$.

parts.label: (h)
parts.text:
A chemical reaction may be speeded up by the presence of a catalyst.

Explain why a catalyst increases the rate of a chemical reaction.
